field.label: Enable scrub
field.help: Enable default packet scrubbing and MSS clamping.

field.label: IP Do-Not-Fragment
field.help: Clear the don't-fragment bit on reassembled IPv4 packets.

field.label: IP Random ID
field.help: Replace predictable IPv4 identification values with random values.

field.label: Skip rules when gateway is down
field.help: By default, when a rule has a specific gateway set and this gateway is down, the rule is created and traffic is sent to the default gateway. This option overrides that behavior and the rule is not created when the gateway is down.

field.label: Sticky connections
field.help: Successive connections are redirected in round-robin fashion while connections from the same source are sent to the same gateway for as long as matching states exist.

field.label: Source tracking timeout
field.help: Set the source tracking timeout for sticky connections in seconds. The default of zero removes source tracking as soon as the state expires.

field.label: Shared forwarding
field.help: Share forwarding decisions between the packet filter, traffic shaper, and captive portal to support policy routing in complex setups.

field.label: Disable force gateway
field.help: Disable automatic rules which force local services to use the assigned interface gateway. The system routing table is used instead.

field.label: Schedule States
field.help: Keep states for existing connections when a schedule expires. By default, matching states are cleared.

field.label: Disable reply-to
field.help: Disable reply-to on WAN rules. This is required for bridged setups where the WAN gateway differs from the gateway used by hosts behind the bridge.

field.label: Disable anti-lockout
field.help: Disable the automatic administration anti-lockout rule. Ensure user-defined rules allow access to the web interface or SSH first.

field.label: Disable RFC4890 requirement rules
field.help: Do not create automatic IPv6 RFC4890 requirement rules.

field.label: Disable port 0 block
field.help: Do not create the automatic rule blocking port 0.

field.label: Disable sshlockout
field.help: Do not create automatic rules blocking failed login attempts. Custom rules can still use the sshlockout table.

field.label: Disable rate limit rule
field.help: Do not create the automatic rule blocking rate-limited sessions. Custom rules can still use the virusprot table.

field.label: Reflection for destination NAT
field.help: When enabled, this automatically creates additional NAT redirect rules for access to port forwards on your external IP addresses from within your internal networks. Individual rules may override this system setting.

field.label: Reflection for 1:1
field.help: Enables the automatic creation of additional NAT redirect rules for access to 1:1 mappings of your external IP addresses from within your internal networks. Individual rules may override this system setting.

field.label: Automatic source NAT for Reflection
field.help: Automatically create source NAT rules which assist destination NAT rules that direct traffic back out to the same subnet it originated from.

field.label: Mode
field.help: Choose how source NAT rules are handled. Automatic mode generates rules for you, hybrid mode combines manual and automatic rules, manual mode only uses configured rules, and disabled mode turns source NAT off.

field.label: Default block
field.help: Log packets matched by the implicit default block rule. Per-rule logging options are still respected.

field.label: Default pass
field.help: Log packets matched by implicit default pass rules. Per-rule logging options are still respected.

field.label: Source NAT
field.help: Log packets matched by automatic source NAT rules.

field.label: Bogon networks
field.help: Log packets blocked by Block Bogon Networks rules.

field.label: Private networks
field.help: Log packets blocked by Block Private Networks rules.

field.label: Bogon Update Frequency
field.help: The frequency of updating the lists of IP addresses that are reserved (but not RFC 1918) or not yet assigned by IANA.
